description: Unscheduled on purpose for the duration of the hackathon: a weekly window means a PR that conflicts sits unrebased for days. Restore a schedule once the pace drops.

customManagers.description: Track the Terraform CLI pin in the Infra workflow. The github-actions manager only updates `uses:` refs, so this version -- which decides what actually runs the apply -- would otherwise silently rot.
Track the gitleaks pin in the Security workflow. Same blind spot as the Terraform pin: the version lives in a workflow env var, which the github-actions manager does not read.

packageRules.description: Bump open `>=` ranges in Python deps. Renovate's default leaves a range alone while the new version still satisfies it, so `flask>=3.1.0` would never produce a PR for 3.2. Neither Python project has a lockfile, so the range is the only place a version is recorded.
Vite and its React plugin gate each other's peer ranges, so separate PRs each fail to resolve a lockfile and land as a red `renovate/artifacts` check. One PR moves them together.

Hold Python at 3.13. The Lambda runtime is pinned to python3.13 in infra/api.tf and build_lambda.sh selects cp313 wheels, so bumping the CI version alone would test on a runtime we do not deploy. Drop this rule when moving all three together.
Group all non-major npm updates into one PR
Group all non-major Python updates into one PR
Keep React and its types in lockstep
The Terraform CLI runs the apply on main -- never let it move without a human reading the plan.
